edges.title: Rubinstein and Villa-Lobos’s first Paris stay, 1923

works.to: Rudepoema, dedicated to Rubinstein, first played by him in 1927

edges.claim: The pianist Arthur Rubinstein met Villa-Lobos in Rio in 1918, included his works in his concert tours and urged wealthy Brazilians to support him. With Rubinstein’s recommendation Villa-Lobos secured funds in 1923 for a first stay in Paris. The money came from the Guinle family; one account names Arnaldo Guinle and another names Carlos Guinle. Villa-Lobos dedicated Rudepoema to Rubinstein, who gave its first performance in 1927.

edges.title: Villa-Lobos’s Bachianas Brasileiras after Bach

works.from: Preludes and fugues of The Well-Tempered Clavier; Mass in B minor

edges.claim: An aunt played preludes and fugues from [[bach|Bach]]’s Well-Tempered Clavier to the young Villa-Lobos, and a manuscript survives of a Bach fugue that he transcribed for cello and piano in 1910. In 1930 he began the Bachianas Brasileiras, nine works in which most movements have a Baroque title and a Brazilian one. In 1935 he gave the Brazilian première of the B minor Mass, and in 1941 he transcribed preludes and fugues from the Forty-Eight for an orchestra of cellos. Simon Wright quotes his description of Bach as “a universal folkloric source”.

sources.title: Simon Wright, note to Hyperion CDA66257 (Villa-Lobos: Bachianas brasileiras Nos 1 & 5)

edges.title: Villa-Lobos’s twelve études for Segovia

works.to: Segovia’s preface to the Eschig edition (January 1953); first performance of the Guitar Concerto, Houston, 1956

edges.claim: Villa-Lobos met Andrés Segovia in Paris in 1924. Segovia asked him for a study, and Villa-Lobos wrote twelve, which Eschig later published with a dedication to Segovia on each. In his preface, dated New York, January 1953, Segovia wrote, in Stanley Yates’s translation, that Villa-Lobos “understood the guitar perfectly” and that his fingerings must be strictly obeyed. Segovia also gave the first performance of the Guitar Concerto in Houston on 6 February 1956; he had held out for several years until the composer supplied a cadenza.

sources.title: John Patykula, “A Look at the 1956 Premiere of Villa-Lobos’ Immortal Concerto for Guitar”, Classical Guitar (Summer 2017)
sources.locator: Segovia asked for an étude and received twelve; the Fantasia concertante, the cadenza and the Houston premiere of 6 February 1956

edges.title: Medeiros’s Yará in Villa-Lobos’s Chôros No. 10

works.from: Yará, schottische for piano, with Catulo da Paixão Cearense’s words as the song Rasga o coração

edges.claim: Chôros No. 10 includes the melody of Yará, a schottische by Anacleto de Medeiros (1866–1907). The poet Catulo da Paixão Cearense had added words to it under the title Rasga o coração, and Villa-Lobos used that title as the subtitle of the Chôros, which was first performed in Rio on 11 November 1926. Catulo’s heirs sued over the use of his words. Villa-Lobos replaced them with a vocalise, and the second edition of the score dropped both the words and the subtitle.

sources.title: Jorge Coli, booklet note to BIS-CD-1520 (Villa-Lobos: Choros Nos 2, 3, 10, 12)
